history.dynasty: Nawabs of Awadh (Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula, 4th Nawab, r. 1775-1797; architect Kifayatullah)
history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: Bara Imambara (Asafi Imambara) is a Shia Muslim imambara - a congregation hall for Azadari (mourning rituals), NOT a Hindu temple - keep-or-drop decision needed. Built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula in 1784 as a famine-relief employment project (built without iron or wood; one of the world's largest arched halls without beams, ~50 m long and ~15 m high). The complex includes the famous Bhool Bhulaiya (labyrinth of ~489 identical doorways), the Asfi Mosque and the Shahi Baoli stepwell, and stands on the banks of the Gomti at Hussainabad, Lucknow.

name: Bara Imambara
town_description: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Gomti river. It was the seat of the Nawabs of Awadh and is famed for its Awadhi culture, cuisine, tehzeeb, and Indo-Islamic architecture such as the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza.

travel.airport: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, Lucknow (~15 km)
travel.road: Hussainabad Road, Chowk, old Lucknow; reachable by taxi, auto-rickshaw and city buses
